Global economic activity remains favourable, although there is considerable uncertainty over future developments.

All in all, monetary policy will continue to be expansionary for a long period of time.

The risks of excessively low inflation merit particular attention, as at the prevailing interest rate levels, excessively low inflation is more difficult to manage than excessively high inflation.

Deputy Governor Martin Flodén entered a reservation against the repo-rate path in the Monetary Policy Report.

He advocated a repo-rate path that indicates it is likely that the repo rate will be raised by 0.25 percentage points at the monetary policy meeting in October, but which coincides with the report's repo-rate path as from the third quarter of 2019.
He thought that the communication of such a repo-rate path would entail sufficient tightening of monetary policy today.
